scope: Source-bound evidence for one observed AC1024 LayerStates graph. The graph is typed and retained for reading, but its XRECORD contains group 370, outside Autodesk’s documented DXF XRECORD application payload domain (1–369 except 5 and 105). Output preparation therefore refuses the graph before queueing it. This receipt does not qualify emitted bytes, fresh DXF readback, LayerStates restoration semantics or whole-source conversion.

observed_graph: DICTIONARY 0xD5 contains ACAD_LAYERFILTERS to 0xEE (238), ACAD_LAYERSTATES to 0x1B8 (440), and ACLYDICTIONARY to 0xED (237).
The two companion dictionaries have no entries and are owned by DICTIONARY 0xD5.
ACAD_LAYERSTATES dictionary 0x1B8 contains ACAD_VIEWS_RenderView to XRECORD 0x249 (585); the XRECORD is owned by 0x1B8 and has typed XDATA values.

autodesk_xrecord_specification.rule: XRECORD application values use group codes 1–369 except 5 and 105; group 370 is outside the documented domain.

cross_check.source: Autodesk ObjectARX Developer Guide, DXF Group Codes for Xrecords
cross_check.rule: The XRECORD-specific code table ends at 360–369 (hard ownership IDs); it defines no code-370 XRECORD payload.

proof: The physical AC1024 graph is identified only from unique source identities and matching standard DWG typed baselines.

The observed XRECORD carries group 370. Since Autodesk’s DXF XRECORD domain ends at 369, output preparation now leaves this graph unprepared and does not add its dictionaries or XRECORD to output queues.
Read retention remains independent of output eligibility. No transformation or custom remapping is inferred for group 370.
The staged inspector can compare exact dictionary/XRECORD bodies and mapped handle roles for a future eligible profile, but it was not reached or qualified for this source.
